title: The Moon Is Leaving Earth, and We Measure It With Lasers

scenes.text: The Moon is leaving. We measure it with lasers.
Apollo 11, 14 and 15 left mirror arrays on the Moon.
Today telescopes on Earth fire lasers at them and time the bounce back.
The round trip tells us the distance, to within centimeters.
The result: the Moon drifts away about 3.8 centimeters every year. About an inch and a half.
Only one photon comes back every few seconds. That's enough to prove it.

description:
The Moon is leaving Earth, and we measure it with lasers.
Telescopes fire laser pulses at mirror arrays left by Apollo 11, 14 and 15 and time the bounce back. The Moon recedes about 3.8 centimeters per year.
What would the sky look like in a billion years?
